criterion: The loader-diag-xnu-ckpt image, started from the RECOVERY slot, fills the kernel copy's XNULDRST slot and jumps to the kernel's own unmodified entry; the kernel's start code reaches its assembly checkpoints, branches to the loader's return stub, the stub draws each arrival and resumes the kernel at checkpoints 1..4, and holds at checkpoint 5 with a report (decision 0016). 'pass' means this expected result was observed; it says nothing beyond checkpoint 5.
summary: One native run of NAT-022 loader-diag-xnu-ckpt (RECOVERY image sha256 b17d0a8c2a25029cc71df874093707706862faf53c3138427b325d72d98d94c1, Image.payload c8ee3a21aa620891da9c1a50da5c6279fe78015b1d8b09560a587f3947d2ed60, loader Image 5d40d6238ea89642e82b097766398abc29205f43150e2eb4413d739d395f368e, source commit 5c7d634, decision commit bca6df3). Written to RECOVERY (/dev/block/sda18) with a matching full readback and booted once (adb reboot recovery at 2026-11-10T20:11:34.4Z = 2026-11-11 01:11 local). The owner filmed the screen (85.9 s, 720x1280). decode_video.py (--y0 10, four windows) decoded 666 CRC-valid frames (CKPT 368, STAGE 118, REG 123, BOOTID 50, ENTRY 7). Order: ENTRY 0x8900; loader STAGE 0x30, 0x31, 0x32, 0x34 and PRE_JUMP 0x40 (20.1-20.9 s; STAGE 0x20, 0x21 and 0x33 were not decoded in this recording, the 0-20 s window has CRC/sync failures, but the later mask shows bits 0-8 set); then CKPT x2:x3 = 0x0201 / mask 0x2 (21.7 s), 0x0202 / 0x6, 0x0203 / 0xe, 0x0204 / 0x1e (to 32.6 s); STAGE 0x51 with STAGE idx1 mask 0x09ff (bits 0-8 and 11, no FAIL bit 9, no NAT-028 stub bit 10); then the held report: CKPT 0x0205, arrival mask 0x3e, arrivals 5, SCTLR_EL1 low32 0x3454599c, TTBR1_EL1 0x0009e15af000, VBAR_EL1 low16 0x7000, TCR_EL1 low32 0xa51a251a, BOOTID 0x6b3c/0x479e, REG block (status 1, GLOBAL_CON lo 0x0133, TRIG_CON 0x3062 -> 0x3063, FRAME_COUNT 0x0ac4 -> 0x0ac5, kicks 0x21). A second complete held report starts at 65.2 s and repeats the same values; the last CRC-valid frame is at 84.2 s, matching the 83 s watchdog. No CKPT arrival with mask bit 8 (early-exception report), bit 9 (x2=0), bit 10 (unexpected arrival) and no FAIL frame. Meaning: the kernel's own, unmodified start code ran on the S24 through five assembly checkpoints; the loader's stub took four arrivals, saved and restored every register and the SP and resumed the kernel each time; the kernel's TTBR1/TCR/VBAR setup and, per the model, its MMU enable lie between checkpoints 4 and 5, then the stub held at 5. The values the kernel wrote (TTBR1_EL1, TCR_EL1, VBAR_EL1) equal the NAT-030 model's predictions exactly; SCTLR_EL1 differs from the model in bits 5 and 7 only. Stock RECOVERY was restored with one NAT-013 session after a physical Download Mode re-entry (bus 5 dev 66, 20:15:35Z-20:15:39Z); Android was back (check_android pass at 20:18:59Z), the full hash equals stock (96620b8b...), assess pass.

sctlr_el1.reading: The kernel's write sets bit 5 (CP15BEN) and leaves bit 7 (ITD) clear; the hardware read-back has them the other way round. The model stores a written value verbatim, without per-bit RES0/RES1 handling. That is consistent with the S24 cores not implementing AArch32 EL0 (those bits are then fixed by the architecture) but this was not checked against the Arm ARM or another read here. M, C and I agree; the difference has no effect on any checkpoint outcome.

established: The kernel's own, unmodified start code executed on the S24: five NAT-029 assembly checkpoint macros were reached in order (CKPT 0x0201..0x0205, arrival masks 0x2, 0x6, 0xe, 0x1e, 0x3e, five arrivals), decoded from CRC-valid frames in two complete held reports. This is the first XNU instruction execution on this device.

The loader's return mechanism works on hardware: the kernel branched through the XNULDRST slot to the loader's stub (arrival frames drawn, so the stub's stack and marker code ran with the kernel's register state saved), and the saved registers and SP were restored and the kernel resumed at the checkpoint's continuation four times (checkpoints 1..4).

The kernel's own register setup ran up to checkpoint 5: at the stop the stub read TTBR1_EL1 0x9e15af000, TCR_EL1 lo32 0xa51a251a, VBAR_EL1 lo16 0x7000 and an SCTLR_EL1 carrying the kernel's configuration (C, I, SA, SA0 and the other kernel-set bits), equal to what the model predicts the kernel has written before checkpoint 5. The model has the kernel set SCTLR.M between checkpoints 4 and 5, so checkpoint 5 was reached with translation on; the hardware read shows M=0 because the checkpoint macro clears it, so MMU-on execution is inferred from the model plus the arrival, not read back directly.

TTBR1_EL1, TCR_EL1 low 32 bits and VBAR_EL1 low 16 bits equal the NAT-030 model's predictions exactly; SCTLR_EL1 agrees on every bit except 5 and 7 (see model_comparison). Neither the kernel's early-exception path (mask bit 8) nor a loader FAIL was observed.

The loader-side hazards of decision 0016 did not materialise: no exception between PRE_JUMP and the first checkpoint, no hang before checkpoint 1, and the display lasted until the 83 s watchdog (last frame 84.2 s). RECOVERY was restored to the pinned stock hash and Android returned with user data directories present.
not_established: Anything the kernel does after checkpoint 5: the stub held there, resuming at 5 needs loader code reachable under the kernel's own TTBR0 map (the kernel's PC is physical and its MMU was on when it reached the macro); arm_init and every C checkpoint are untested (C checkpoint 10 is known from the host model to fault on a NULL boot-args pointer; the first safe C checkpoint is 11).
That the ADT and boot_args are acceptable to XNU beyond the first 8202 model steps of the start code (the real start code reached checkpoint 5 here, which is consistent with the model, nothing more).
Why SCTLR_EL1 bits 5 and 7 differ from the model (hypothesis only: architecture-fixed bits when AArch32 EL0 is absent); no other register read or comparison was made.
Instruction-fetch and cache coherence in the kernel's own MMU-on phase beyond the evidence that execution continued to checkpoint 5; memory attributes of the window under the kernel's page tables.
A transport independent of the screen, the GPU/display path of the kernel, SMP, interrupts, timers: nothing of these ran.
Frames STAGE 0x20, 0x21, 0x33 were not decoded in this recording; the loader's reach of those stages is inferred from the mask 0x09ff (bits 0-8) only.
What caused the Download Mode entries before the restore (owner action; no USB observer was running).
